This optimization speeds up exclusive memory accesses by the guest program.
Enabling it reduces the overhead of fastmem failure of exclusive memory accesses.

This optimization speeds up memory accesses by allowing invalid memory accesses to succeed.
Enabling it reduces the overhead of all memory accesses and has no impact on programs that don't access invalid memory.

This optimization speeds up memory accesses by the guest program.
Enabling it causes guest memory reads/writes to be done directly into memory and make use of Host's MMU.
Disabling this forces all memory accesses to use Software MMU Emulation.

This optimization speeds up memory accesses by the guest program.
Enabling it inlines accesses to PageTable::pointers into emitted code.
Disabling this forces all memory accesses to go through the Memory::Read/Memory::Write functions.

When enabled, a misalignment is only triggered when an access crosses a page boundary.
When disabled, a misalignment is triggered on all misaligned accesses.
Enable a two-tiered dispatch system. A faster dispatcher written in assembly has a small MRU cache of jump destinations is used first. If that fails, dispatch falls back to the slower C++ dispatcher.
Enables an IR optimization that reduces unnecessary accesses to the CPU context structure.
Enables IR optimizations that involve constant propagation.
This optimization avoids dispatcher lookups by allowing emitted basic blocks to jump directly to other basic blocks if the destination PC is static.
This optimization avoids dispatcher lookups by keeping track potential return addresses of BL instructions. This approximates what happens with a return stack buffer on a real CPU.
